question: Does a GLOBAL allocation beat uniform allocation at equal total model-specific bytes, measured in function space on real held-out activations, once the non-MLP floors dominate the implied 2.9398 EBPW?

implied_whole_model_floor_ebpw.null: a uniform-per-organ mix is not a measured whole-model floor

non_mlp_floor_if_mlp_zero_ebpw.null: not a proposal to delete the MLP
non_mlp_floor_if_mlp_zero_ebpw.note: even if MLP went to zero bits the other three organs still cost this

capture.hold_cap_rule: real hold split from the capture manifest; uniformly subsampled to 768 rows with seed 20260824. Not a Gaussian draw, not a fit leak.

accounting_rules.rule: A 16-bit scale per group of 64 is 0.25 bpw, not free. Report storage AND active, or neither. Island ids are 32-bit.

quality.capability_proxy: scale_aware = cosine * gain, on held-out real Y = X W^T
quality.rejects_0p01W: cosine(Y, 0.01Y) ~ 1, gain ~ 0.01, rel_fro ~ 0.99; GO uses scale_aware/gain/rel_fro, never cosine alone

uniform.rule: every allocatable tensor at the same storage_bpw, interpolated on its dense RD curve

model.note: Incumbent measured 448 GB/s against a 595.9 GB/s roof. Scaling TOKEN_NS with active bytes is the bandwidth-bound model GPU_LEDGER ranks above stored size. Positive extra active bytes LOWER tok/s.

throughput.null: a Metal complete-wall of this mix; GPU_LEDGER measured the q4 incumbent only

verdict.reading: GLOBAL beats whole-model uniform at equal bytes (weighted scale_aware 0.825636 vs 0.724711). The floors are tradeable. GLOBAL also beats the implied-floor per-organ mix at the same total bytes — layer- and tensor-heterogeneity (and any island that paid) is worth spending against a uniform-per-organ budget. Allocated storage_bpw spans 1.250 .. 4.367 (span 3.117). That is the point of a global allocator, not a rounding of a uniform budget.
